rows.name: Kahuku Land Farms Stand
rows.neighborhood: Kahuku (across from Kawela Bay, near Turtle Bay Resort)
rows.schedule_text: <cite index="1-5,1-6">A 2017 Star-Advertiser piece places the stand on Kamehameha Highway, mauka side, across the Kawela Bay entrance, and says it is open daily during daylight hours.</cite> Not confirmed as current by any own page or organizer.
rows.description: <cite index="1-9,1-10">A collective of roadside stands, loosely known as Kahuku Land Farms, selling bags of cut fruit and whole fruit.</cite> <cite index="1-11">Most of the produce is grown on farms just behind the stand, on land leased out by Turtle Bay Resort (as of 2017).</cite>
rows.notes: No own website, social account or organizer found. Street address left null: the 56-800 Kamehameha Hwy address on an aggregator is Kahuku Farms' address, and a map-app address and phone were not used because they come from map listings. Kuilima Farm's own site says its farm stand is mauka of the Ritz-Carlton Oʻahu, Turtle Bay, across from Kawela Bay (https://kuilimafarm.com/experience), so the two stand clusters may overlap, but nothing ties this collective to Kuilima. Fodor's describes the Kuilima Farm Stand as having multiple stalls. A Honolulu Magazine road trip (about Aug 2026) says the writers browsed neighboring stands next to Kuilima Farm Stand, which suggests roadside stands still operate there, but it does not name this collective. A Hawaiʻi Life guide (about Mar 2026) lists 'Kahuku Fruit Stands' open daily 9-5 and ties them to Kahuku Farms, which conflicts with the independent-stand description, so that schedule was not used. still_active is null: nearby stands appear to be operating but this collective is not confirmed. Duplicate of the next row; they should be merged in the directory.

rows.name: Kahuku Land Farms Stand (Kahuku fruit stands)
rows.schedule_text: A 2017 Star-Advertiser piece said open daily during daylight hours. Not confirmed as current.
rows.description: <cite index="1-9">A collective loosely known as the Kahuku Land Farms stand, on Kamehameha Highway across from the Kawela Bay entrance.</cite> Sells cut fruit, whole fruit and coconuts per the 2017 article.
rows.notes: Duplicate of the previous row (same source, same findings); recommend listing once. No own page, organizer or social account found and no usable street address. Only the 2017 article describes this collective by name. Honolulu Magazine (about Aug 2026) mentions neighboring stands beside Kuilima Farm Stand, but the operator and current hours of this collective are unverified. The 9-5 daily schedule in the Hawaiʻi Life guide is attributed there to Kahuku Farms, so it was not used. Kuilima Farm Stand's own site lists 9am-5pm daily at 57-146 Kamehameha Hwy; it is a separate listing and was not merged.

rows.name: Local Inside CSA (Hawaii Agricultural Foundation, HAF Ag Park Kunia)
rows.venue_name: HAF Ag Park, Kunia (produce source); pickup sites around Oʻahu
rows.schedule_text: No current schedule or pickup sites found. <cite index="78-2">Hawaii Magazine reports HAF launched the Local Inside CSA in 2015.</cite> That article is older.
rows.description: <cite index="78-3">Older coverage says bags were filled with produce grown at the HAF Ag Park in Kunia by small farmers leasing land there.</cite> <cite index="81-1">GoFarm Hawaii says Local Inside, previously a CSA program, now serves as a platform connecting farmers with the community.</cite>
rows.source_label: Hawaii Agricultural Foundation website (contact and farmers pages, ©2025); GoFarm Hawaii; Hawaii Magazine (older)
rows.notes: HAF itself is active: its own site (©2025) describes the Ag Park at Kunia as supporting growers on Central Oʻahu and lists contact info (info@hawaiiagfoundation.org, (808) 927-9749, office at 3538 Waialae Ave #203, Honolulu; the office is not a pickup venue). <cite index="19-4">An HSTA article (about Oct 2026) says HAF is recruiting for its 2026-2027 teacher cohort.</cite> The retrieved HAF pages did not mention a Local Inside CSA bag or pickup program. Together with the GoFarm statement (about 2024) that Local Inside became a platform, the bag-and-pickup model may no longer run. Pickup sites are unverified, so side is null (the Ag Park is in Kunia, central Oʻahu, but pickups were elsewhere). kind is null because none of the allowed kinds fits a CSA. A LocalHarvest listing (old) gave small and large bag prices; those are not current and were not used. still_active is null: the organization is active but the CSA/pickup program is unconfirmed. Not suitable to list as a recurring pickup until HAF confirms.

rows.name: Mahiku Farmers Market
rows.description: <cite index="24-1,24-2">A 2019 directory entry describes a year-round open-air market of local farmers, growers, artisans and food purveyors.</cite> That listing is dated and unverified.
rows.notes: <cite index="26-2">The organizer's contact page gives 41-1009 Mahiku Pl, Waimanalo, HI 96795, contact Sonny Doung at 808-225-4002, and info@mahikufarmersmarket.com.</cite> The page has no schedule or events and no visible date. Weekday hours on aggregator pages appear to come from map listings, so they were not used. <cite index="24-3">The October 2019 directory entry also listed Hyatt Regency Waikīkī (Tue/Thu) and Mililani (Fri) locations.</cite> Those are old and unverified. <cite index="25-6">vendorsmap.com lists the market as seasonal, contact organizer for schedule.</cite> Marketspread asks whether the market is still operational. No evidence it is active in 2026, so still_active is null. Verify with the organizer before publishing. Waimānalo is windward Oʻahu and borderline for an 'east' label.

rows.name: OK Poultry (farm egg sales)
rows.schedule_text: <cite index="32-14">Per an Onolicious Hawaiʻi post, the farm is only open Wednesday and Saturday.</cite> <cite index="36-12">A farm directory lists 7:30am to 1pm on those days.</cite> <cite index="32-13">The blog says to arrive before about 8:30am because eggs sell out.</cite> Not confirmed by a current first-party source.
rows.description: <cite index="30-17,30-18">Eggs are bought directly at the farm; look for the OK Poultry sign on Kakaina Street.</cite> <cite index="33-5">Honolulu Magazine (older) describes a rustic shop with antiques and bins of produce from Waimānalo farmers.</cite>
rows.source_label: Onolicious Hawaiʻi food blog (about 2 years old); localmeatmilkeggs.org directory; Honolulu Magazine (older)
rows.notes: <cite index="30-26">The Onolicious OK Poultry post lists the address, phone 808-259-7832 and instagram.com/okpoultry.</cite> The Instagram URL is built from that blog's handle and was not checked on the platform itself. <cite index="36-10,36-11,36-12">The directory localmeatmilkeggs.org lists the same address and phone, open 7:30 am to 1 pm on Wednesday and Saturday.</cite> <cite index="33-4">Honolulu Magazine confirms the KK Poultry to OK Poultry ownership change.</cite> <cite index="31-2">A Nextdoor business page lists K K Poultry Farm Inc, same phone, with OK Poultry/Waimana TKG as its retail brand.</cite> A directory lists okpoultry.com but I could not verify it, so website is null. Old price ($15 per tray of 30 medium white eggs) was not used. No current first-party page or dated 2026 post was found, so still_active is null. Yelp was not used. Waimānalo is windward and borderline for an 'east' label.

rows.name: Waiahole Farm
rows.description: <cite index="44-4">A TikTok discover page (updated 2026-10-26) describes Waiahole Farm as offering fresh-cut fruit, juices and seasonal tropical fruit on the Windward side.</cite>
rows.source_label: TikTok discover page (aggregated social mention, not the business's own account)
rows.notes: Still a single social mention with no address, hours, handle or organizer. Address candidates appear only on review or map sites, which were not used. A Blue Diamond Vacations blog describes a Waiahole Farm in Waiahole Valley with taro (kalo) fields, and I could not confirm it is the same business as the fruit stand. Waiahole Nursery & Garden Center (own site waiaholenursery.com, 48-190 Kamehameha Hwy) and Waiahole Poi Factory are separate businesses. Needs a first-party source before it goes in the directory. still_active is null.

rows.name: Waialua Fresh Egg Farm (farm stand)
rows.venue_name: Waialua Fresh Egg Farm (listed in Honolulu Magazine as Villa Rose Egg Farm)
rows.schedule_text: Sources disagree and the farm's own site was not retrieved. <cite index="56-5">Honolulu Magazine (March 2025 update) lists Friday to Sunday, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.</cite> <cite index="54-4">A shopper's TikTok post (page updated 2026-09-21) says Thursday to Sunday, 8AM-5PM.</cite> <cite index="57-1,57-3">A Haleiwa Town guide says it is usually open until eggs sell out.</cite> Confirm hours with the farm.
rows.description: <cite index="57-15,57-16">Sells fresh cage-free eggs straight from the farm at 65-1001 Kaukonahua Rd, Waialua.</cite> Sells eggs, not fruit.
rows.source_label: Honolulu Magazine, 'Where to Buy Local Farm-Fresh Eggs on Oʻahu' (March 2025 update); Haleiwa Town guide; TikTok shopper post (Sept 2026)
rows.notes: Address confirmed by Honolulu Magazine and the Haleiwa Town guide. Hours conflict as shown above, and no own page with stand hours was retrieved. Review and map listings were excluded, including the phone number found only there. The farm is operating: WATTAgNet (about Aug 2025) reported four new barns under construction, and Civil Beat (2023) reported an active farm. <cite index="54-4">A September 2026 TikTok post from a shopper who picked up eggs there</cite> supports the stand being open, so still_active is true. This is a recent third-party sign, not an owner confirmation, and confidence is medium. The farm is jointly owned by Hidden Villa Ranch and Rose Acre Farms (Civil Beat). <cite index="57-12,57-13">The Haleiwa Town guide also lists a separate 'Waialua Fresh' produce and pantry stand at 67-071 Nauahi St, Waialua, open daily 9 AM to 6 PM.</cite> I did not tie it to this egg stand and did not merge it. A shopper-reported price was not recorded as admission.
